biography.plain_text: Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani was Qatar's Amir from 1995 to 2013. Sandhurst-trained, he rose through the armed forces before becoming heir apparent and assuming the throne. His reign reshaped Qatar's institutions and international presence, while the Qatar Foundation and Education City made education, research and culture a durable part of his public legacy.

long_biography.plain_text:
Military formation came before rule for Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani. After studying at Sandhurst, he joined Qatar's armed forces, eventually becoming heir apparent and defence minister. He assumed power in 1995 and began a wide programme of institutional development, including a permanent constitution, expanded public infrastructure and a more active diplomatic presence.

Education gave that state-building project a lasting civic dimension. With Sheikha Moza bint Nasser, he established Qatar Foundation, whose Education City brought international universities, research centres and community programmes to Doha. In 2013, he handed authority to his son Tamim, completing a voluntary transition that continued the public institutions built during his reign.
